section_summary: A November 1948 Tokyo despatch forwards a SCAP memorandum easing restrictions on the transfer of securities issued by restricted Japanese concerns. Most of the section consists of repeated copies of April 1948 tables recording stock sales through liquidation agencies, including methods of sale, share counts, proceeds, and the companies whose shares were sold. The final copy continues beyond page 80.

people.name: E. G. Seidensticker Jr.
people.role: Identified by initials on the November 1948 despatch; position not stated.

people.name: Takahashi Kyuroku
people.role: Named in the firm name Takahashi Kyuroku & Co.; no personal role stated.

subfiles.title: Forwarding SCAP memorandum on securities of restricted concerns
subfiles.from: Acting Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAPIN 403/1 and explains its changes to controls on restricted concerns' securities.
subfiles.summary: The despatch summarizes new exemptions for small concerns, limited transfers by financial institutions and dealers, and shareholders' pre-emptive rights. It relates those changes to earlier SCAP directives, Imperial Ordinance 567, and the Antimonopoly Law.

subfiles.title: Disposal and Acquisition of Securities of Restricted Concerns
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Amends restrictions on transfers of securities issued by restricted concerns.
subfiles.summary: SCAPIN 403/1 exempts transfers involving concerns with share capital below ¥5 million and permits specified transfers involving larger concerns, subject to ownership limits and other laws. It also permits certain sales by banks and insurers, dealings by registered brokers, and exercise of pre-emptive rights.

subfiles.title: Securities held by liquidation agencies
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Tabulates securities held by liquidation agencies as of March 1948.
subfiles.summary: Lists categories, share counts, and yen values of securities held by liquidation agencies.

subfiles.title: Sales of Securities Through Liquidation Agencies, enclosure no. 2
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Records shares disposed of through Japanese liquidation agencies up to February 21, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Opening tables total sales by S.C.L.C., H.C.L.C., and C.I.L.C. and distinguish public sales, employee and local resident allocations, and tenders. Detailed company lists then record shares offered and sold, buyers, and proceeds across 1947 and early 1948. The enclosure ends with separate lists for C.I.L.C. and H.C.L.C. disposals.

subfiles.title: Sales of Securities Through Liquidation Agencies, enclosure no. 2, second copy
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Repeats the tables of share disposals through liquidation agencies up to February 21, 1948.
subfiles.summary: This is another OCR copy of the enclosure on pages 6–28. It repeats agency totals, S.C.L.C. sales by period and method, detailed sales by issuing company, and C.I.L.C. and H.C.L.C. disposition lists. OCR quality varies and some figures differ in transcription.

subfiles.title: Sales of Securities Through Liquidation Agencies, enclosure no. 2, third copy
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Repeats the agency totals and company-by-company stock disposal tables.
subfiles.summary: A third copy again gives the cumulative totals through February 21, 1948, followed by S.C.L.C. sale records and C.I.L.C. and H.C.L.C. lists. It includes methods of disposition, numbers of shares, and proceeds. Several figures and names are distorted by OCR.

subfiles.title: Sales of Securities Through Liquidation Agencies, enclosure no. 2, fourth copy
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Begins another copy of the liquidation-agency stock sales enclosure.
subfiles.summary: These pages repeat the cumulative agency totals and the beginning of the S.C.L.C. company-by-company sales list. The copy starts with a summary through February 21, 1948, and reaches August 1947 transactions by page 80. The document continues beyond this section.
